name: UT-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -17 point partisan lean
Incumbent Mike Kennedy has a massive fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price the Republican at 95%
Democratic challenger has minimal cash on hand
model.rationale: The district's -17 point partisan lean, Kennedy's overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing the Republican at 95% all point to a safe Republican hold. No polls or expert ratings suggest any reason to move away from the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected national Democratic wave environment could narrow the margin, though a Republican loss remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Utah's 4th District is a heavily Republican seat, with a partisan lean of 17 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Mike Kennedy is running for reelection and holds a dominant financial position, having raised nearly $1 million while Democrat Jonny Larsen has raised about $54,000 with almost nothing left on hand. Prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 95% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

With no public polling and no signs of a serious Democratic effort, the race rests on fundamentals that all favor Kennedy. The main uncertainty is the size of the Republican margin, not the outcome.
